title: Properness descends along a field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme]. If the base change $X_K:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change] is proper over $K$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], then $X$ is proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: By [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover], the structure morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a flat, surjective, quasi-compact morphism and its singleton family is an fpqc covering. The base change of the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ along this cover is the structure morphism $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, which is proper by hypothesis.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L1 (lemma-descending-property-proper), setup and the one-member fpqc covering Spec(K) -> Spec(k)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-separated] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the singleton cover from step 1. Its base change is separated because a proper morphism is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Hence $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L1, using the separatedness part of the fpqc-locality criterion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-universally-closed] to the same morphism and cover. The base change $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is universally closed because it is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Therefore $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is universally closed.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L1, using the universally-closed part of the fpqc-locality criterion

proof.text: The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type by the hypothesis that $X$ is a scheme of finite type over $k$, which by definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] means that its structure morphism is of finite type. Combining finite type with separatedness from step 2 and universal closedness from step 3, the definition of proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] gives that $X$ is proper over $k$.
